julie: Hi! First day here. Running Ubuntu 22.04 on a ThinkPad, using NetworkManager WireGuard profile (split tunnel). Trying to apt-get update against apt.internal.redwood but it times out. Public apt mirrors are fine. Any quick checks I should run?

infra-jen: welcome! Quick checks: `ip addr`, `ip route`, and `sudo tcpdump -i <iface> port 443` while you try `curl -v https://apt.internal.redwood/` to see which interface/next-hop is used. Also paste `nmcli connection show --active` so we can see the current vpn profile.

julie: outputs: `ip route` shows default via 192.168.0.1 dev wlan0, and a 10.20.0.0/16 dev wg0 route. `nmcli` shows the wg connection active. tcpdump on wg0 shows no packets when I curl, tcpdump on wlan0 shows SYN going out to 10.20.12.5 (our registry host) then RST from gateway.

matt: sounds like policy routing issue where conntrack or Docker is routing via the wrong table. Docker's bridge sometimes bypasses the wg table. Are you running docker containers attempting apt inside the container or on host?

julie: on host (trying to install a package before building image).

matt: okay. Quick remedy: add a host route for the internal subnet to force it over wg0: `sudo ip route add 10.20.0.0/16 dev wg0` (replace if you already have one). If that errors, try `sudo ip rule add from <your-host-ip> table 51820` and `sudo ip route add default dev wg0 table 51820`. That pins traffic from your host to the wg table. If you want a persistent fix, add post-up scripts in NetworkManager keyfile for the WG connection.

julie: adding `ip route add 10.20.0.0/16 dev wg0` succeeded and apt-get now connects. Thank you!!

ops-sre: created ticket INF-998: "nm w/wireguard split-tunnel - onboarding route gaps" assigned to eng-infra. Tagging networking team to review NetworkManager keyfile templates for new hires.

bastion-bot: bastion proxy available: `ssh -D 1080 julie@bastion.internal` if you prefer a proxy path.

julie: good to know. I'll add the `ip rule` snippet to the onboarding checklist so other Linux new hires don't hit this. Appreciate the help! :wave:
